summary_paragraph: The patient with prior Roux-en-Y gastric bypass and known gastrojejunal (marginal) ulcer was directly admitted for inability to tolerate adequate oral intake with persistent nausea/vomiting, epigastric pain requiring opioid analgesia, and significant recent weight loss consistent with moderate protein-calorie malnutrition. She received IV fluids and peripheral parenteral nutrition initially, then underwent uncomplicated tunneled double-lumen central venous catheter placement and was advanced to goal total parenteral nutrition by hospital day 3, subsequently tolerating cycling (16 hours inpatient) and transitioning to a planned 12-hour nocturnal cycle for home with visiting services for line care and lab monitoring. She was maintained on IV pantoprazole (Protonix) for ulcer healing and continued sucralfate; Nutrition provided diet education to support gradual oral intake. Chronic pain consultation recommended adjustments to her as-needed pain regimen with outpatient pain clinic follow-up coordinated through her primary care provider. New right upper quadrant pain was evaluated with ultrasound showing no cholelithiasis or acute cholecystitis. She was discharged home in stable condition, ambulatory, tolerating a stage 5 diet in small amounts, with controlled symptoms and clear return precautions.
problems: Gastrojejunal ulcer, unspecified as acute or chronic, without mention of hemorrhage or perforation, without mention of obstruction
